concept.title: Scalability and minimum requirements
concept.shortdesc: Red Hat Quay scales from proof of concept to large deployments such as Quay.io. You can use sample sizing tables and subscription guidance to plan capacity for your environment.

conbody.p: Scalability of Red Hat Quay is one of its key strengths, with a single code base supporting a broad spectrum of deployment sizes, including the following:

ul.li: Proof of Concept deployment on a single development machine
Mid-size deployment of approximately 2,000 users that can serve content to dozens of Kubernetes clusters
High-end deployment such as Quay.io that can serve thousands of Kubernetes clusters world-wide

conbody.p: Sizing depends on many factors, such as the number of users, images, concurrent pulls and pushes, so standard sizing recommendations are not available.
The following are the minimum requirements for systems running Red Hat Quay (per container/pod instance):

ul.li: Quay: minimum 6 GB; recommended 8 GB, 2 or more vCPUs
Clair: recommended 2 GB RAM and 2 or more vCPUs
NooBaa: minimum 2 GB, 1 vCPU (when you select the objectstorage component in the Operator)
Clair database: minimum 5 GB required for security metadata

conbody.p: Stateless components of Red Hat Quay can be scaled out, but scaling increases load on stateful backend services.
